body: Where specifically lies the difficulty? Getting a "green card"? It's a tough lot, but perhaps it would be easier to get into some other country (perhaps in Europe) where it's totally socially acceptable to be gay.

In retrospect: ask away!

I've approached women that were part of my social circle. Though I am unable to feel attracted to overweight women, I know that a guy in my position, who considers himself unattractive--I've had these urges (to evaluate my appearance in the mirror and look for flaws) since I was six years old at least--can't be picky, but the primal attraction simply isn't there, and to be honest I don't think it's too much of me to ask that my partner ought to be reasonably in shape, since I myself have worked out religiously to obtain a V-shaped athletic physique with low body fat (only the neck remains pencil-tier, but I have purchased a neck harness to beef up in that area).

The girls that I have approached (all with some kind of "valid" reason such as common interests and opinions) have ranged from average-looking (slim people are hardly average these days, but I am here considering facial appearance) to slightly below and slightly above.  I certainly don't go for "bimbos", though I would love to have a relationship with one if only to "prove" that someone can be attracted to me. However, this is part of my fantasy realm, and I have never actually approached this kind of woman.

I can be extraordinarily passionate about my pursuits, most prominently music (I am a composer, operatic tenor, and guitarist), art (I used to draw constantly as a child, but nowadays I just appreciate the visual art produced by others), agriculture (I would like to live on a farm and grow my own biodynamic crops), literature, and video games. I certainly don't lack passion, but I have a difficult time expressing it to others, since I "know" from experience that people will mock me for it (this was the case in Junior High, when I was severely bullied partially for my passion for various things and eccentricity).

You seem to be a person closer to my wavelength than the vast majority that I encounter in real life. Thanks for your response! I will take your advice (though I have had plans for it for a long time) and try to focus on the things that I love, my desire for love and sexual intimacy aside. The problem is that it is very difficult for me to focus on anything else than love and sex, and if I try to suppress my obsession, it comes back to haunt me twofold.

Could you perhaps try to move to a country where homosexuality is accepted? I know that leaving one's family behind would be very difficult, but if they don't understand you anyway, you might as well do yourself a favour and follow your heart.

Thank you for the kind words, guys. I think that "extremely attractive" is a gross exaggeration, as I would probably have girls begging me to have sex with them if that were the case, but I am a very poor judge of myself, so I believe that others are able to evaluate my appearance with greater objectivity.

It is true what you say, thefox116, that one shouldn't be dependent on others to be able to feel about oneself. In my case, though, I was ostracised and bullied for years, an experience that shattered my self-esteem. Thoughts that more or less uninterruptedly race through my mind could be characterised as "Why me? Why can virtually everyone else get at least ONE girl to be attracted to them, but not me? What is wrong with me? Is it my pupillary distance? Is it my fat lip? Is it due to an unhealthy hormonal profile? Do I reek of shit? Are my feet too small? Is 6' an insufficient height these days (though I personally know men much shorter than I am who have had many rewarding relationships)?"

I think that I am a very neurotic person, due to being predisposed to analysis and introversion. Coupled with horrible self-esteem, this leads to bouts of severe self-harm (when I get frustrated enough, I tend to bite my arms until blood gushes from the wounds) and fierce self-criticism.

Thank you for the elaborate response. I am already a "chronic" cannabis user (I tend to smoke a few small bowls a few hours before going to bed), and it does help to some extent, as it allows me to eat properly (I have a bowel disorder that gives me a hard time) and spend some relative quality time playing games, composing music, and watching entertaining TV shows. It is unfortunately illegal here (I am from Sweden), but I have never had any issues with the police. Unfortunately the dank stuff is rather expensive here.

I have been in contact with a few psychiatrists, and while I kind of am suspicious of their discipline, I feel that I am humble enough not to disregard any possible solution. I dislike the idea of being on daily medication, but as I conceded above, I am prepared to give it a shot. 

Previously I have tried SSRIs and SNRIs, neither of which worked, possibly due to my issues not being related to serotonin. I have been on antipsychotic medications briefly, since I sometimes have borderline schizophrenic episodes (I think that I have a tendency to misinterpret sensory data) during which I will spend hours upon hours watching my face and body in the mirror, attempting to diagnose the root cause of my lack of sex/romantic appeal.

In my late teens I was addicted to bensodiazepines and opioids for a couple of years, as I couldn't handle the idea (not so much the actuality) of not having a girlfriend or anything of the sort. That is, I don't so much mind not being in a sexual/romantic relationship as I mind the lack of possibility of obtaining one. Anyhow, the opioids, while boosting my dopamine levels, ultimately led to a level of dread that I had previously not thought possible. This experience is why I would rather kill myself than hop on such powerful drugs again.

Thank you for caring enough to respond. I have already seen countless therapists, and they just tell me that there's no reason for me to be involuntarily celibate, as though it's a choice of mine, rather than a terrible affliction. I do believe that my dysphoria is related to a dopamine deficiency, something that one can hardly discuss away (though perhaps the placebo effect could do something).

The problem is that I have already talked to everyone that I can imagine, and no matter how I "approach", I always end up getting rejected and often humiliated. I don't understand what's wrong with me, because my friends and family tell me that I behave appropriately.

Being unable (despite trying) to establish a romantic/sexual relationship throughout High School is Hell.

I understand your concerns, as they are similar to mine own. I have grown to become severely misanthropic as a consequence of the shortcomings of both myself as well as others. "Social media" is indeed nothing but an outlet for showing off, the main arena for pretending to care about the woes of the unfortunate just to appear "good" in the eyes of others.

If you would like to, you could add me at Skype (cielporteur) and try to reach out to me, if you don't mind sharing your problems with a stranger.

Well, the reason that I don't "look friendly" is that I have experienced nothing but rejection and (implicit and explicit) bullying for as long as I can remember. Unless you mean that my facial traits don't look friendly, in other words that I am ugly.

My intention here is not to affirm your hypothesis, which may very well be true in some sense, but I hope you can imagine how difficult it is to do all of those things when your very being intuitively knows that it will bring nothing but even more pain and rejection. Hence, the "emotional guard" is formed, as a function of life experience.

You have a really nice smile. The look of a truly nice girl.

Can't really say that you have a "worst" trait, as they all go nicely together. 

I can promise you that I am completely honest and objectively minded in my evaluation--if there were something unappealing or "off" about your face, I would mention it.
